q: Which timber is known as "Philippine Mahogany"?
n: Tanguile (Shorea polysperma) is the Philippine timber sold as Philippine mahogany. Guijo and yakal are harder structural species and are not sold under that name.
ref: PNS/DENR Philippine timber species list - Shorea polysperma (tanguile); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood

q: Which wood joint has a projecting tongue that fits into a cut socket and is widely used in door and window frames?
n: In a mortise and tenon joint the tenon fits into the mortise, giving a strong frame joint.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood joinery

q: Which wood joint uses interlocking wedge-shaped tails and resists being pulled apart, as in drawers?
n: The flared tails lock mechanically against pull-out, which is why drawers use them.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood joinery

q: Which wood joint joins two members at their ends by cutting each at 45° to make a right-angle corner, as in picture frames?
n: A miter joint hides the end grain by cutting both pieces at half the corner angle.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood joinery

q: Which wood joint is made by removing half the thickness of each member so they overlap and lie flush?
n: In a lap joint the two members overlap and the surfaces stay flush.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood joinery

q: Which wood joint is typically used for flooring boards, with a projecting edge fitting into a groove?
n: The tongue of one board fits the groove of the next, so the floor stays aligned.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood flooring and joinery

q: Liquid Tile is a paint product line of which Philippine paint manufacturer?
n: Liquid Tile is a Davies Paints product line.
ref: Davies Paints Philippines - Liquid Tile product line

q: What glass thickness is generally used for a frameless tempered glass door with patch fittings?
n: Frameless doors with patch fittings use 10 to 12 mm tempered glass, because the fittings clamp the glass itself and carry the door weight.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - glass and glazing, frameless tempered doors

q: Spider fittings are used to support what kind of glazing?
o: Point-fixed frameless glass such as facades and canopies
n: Spider fittings hold the glass at its corners with bolts through holes in the glass, so no frame is needed.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - point-fixed structural glazing

q: How does an awning window operate?
o: It is hinged at the side and swings like a door
It is hinged at the top and swings outward at the bottom
It slides horizontally on a track
It pivots on a center axis
n: An awning window is top-hung with friction stays. A casement window is side-hung.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - windows, operation types

q: Which CHB type is U-shaped so that reinforcement and grout can form a horizontal beam over openings?
n: A lintel (bond-beam) block has a U-shaped channel for horizontal bars and grout.
ref: PNS ASTM C90:2019 / C129:2019 - concrete masonry units; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - concrete masonry units

q: Which CHB type has one flat end so that it can finish a wall corner or wall end?
n: A corner block has a solid, flat end for an exposed corner or end.
ref: PNS ASTM C90:2019 / C129:2019 - concrete masonry units; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - concrete masonry units

q: Which CHB type is half the length of a standard block and is used to finish courses at ends or offsets?
n: A half block fills the space where a full block will not fit and maintains the running bond.
ref: PNS ASTM C90:2019 / C129:2019 - concrete masonry units; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - concrete masonry units

q: Which CHB type has a rounded exposed edge and is used at wall corners and openings?
n: A bullnose block has a rounded arris, which gives a safer and softer corner.
ref: PNS ASTM C90:2019 / C129:2019 - concrete masonry units; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - concrete masonry units

q: Mactan stone, a common building and cladding stone, is a type of what?
n: Mactan stone is a coralline limestone quarried in Cebu.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - stone; Philippine dimension stone practice, Mactan coralline limestone

q: Which stone is a sedimentary limestone with characteristic pitted holes and is often used for wall and floor cladding?
n: Travertine is formed from mineral springs, and its natural voids are often filled and polished.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - stone, travertine

q: Adobe stone in the Philippines is a type of what?
n: Adobe stone is a soft volcanic tuff that is easy to cut into blocks.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - stone; Philippine adobe (volcanic tuff) practice

q: Which concrete work is identified as concrete pneumatically sprayed at high velocity onto a surface?
n: Shotcrete is sprayed concrete, used for tunnels, slopes and retaining walls.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - concrete placement, shotcrete

q: What is a power trowel used for?
o: Finishing the surface of a concrete slab
n: A power trowel is a rotating-blade machine for smoothing and finishing slabs.
ref: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate - concrete equipment and finishing

q: Which concrete term refers to concrete batched at a plant and delivered in a truck mixer?
n: Ready-mix is batched off-site and delivered to the project, usually by transit mixer.
ref: ASTM C94 / PNS - ready-mixed concrete; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed.

q: What is a plate compactor used for?
n: A plate compactor is a vibrating base plate that densifies granular fill.
ref: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate - earthwork compaction equipment

q: What is retained on a 5 mm (No. 4) sieve?
n: Material retained on the 4.75 mm (No. 4) sieve is coarse aggregate. Material passing it is fine aggregate.
ref: ASTM C33 - concrete aggregates, 4.75 mm (No. 4) sieve

q: Which cement type is the general-purpose cement used for ordinary construction?
n: Ordinary Portland cement (Type I) is the general-purpose type.
ref: ASTM C150 / PNS 07 - portland cement types

q: Which cement has lower heat of hydration and is favored for mass concrete, marine works and sulfate-attack resistance?
n: The pozzolanic reaction is slower and gives off less heat, so it suits mass and marine work.
ref: ASTM C595 / PNS 63 - blended hydraulic (pozzolan) cement

q: Which cement gains strength very quickly and resists high temperatures and chemical attack?
n: High alumina cement gives rapid strength gain and is used for refractory and chemical-resistant applications.
ref: ASTM C1721 - calcium aluminate (high alumina) cement

q: What is the minimum concrete cover for concrete cast against and permanently in contact with the ground (NSCP 2015)?
n: For concrete cast against and permanently in contact with the ground, the cover is 75 mm.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 420.6.1.3.1 - specified concrete cover

q: What is the minimum concrete cover for beams and columns not exposed to weather or ground (NSCP 2015)?
n: Beams and columns need 40 mm of cover to the main bars, ties and stirrups. Slabs, walls and joists with bars No. 36 and smaller need only 20 mm.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 420.6.1.3.1 - specified concrete cover

q: What is the minimum concrete cover for slabs, walls and joists with No. 36 and smaller bars, not exposed to weather or ground (NSCP 2015)?
n: Slabs, walls and joists with bars No. 36 and smaller need 20 mm of cover.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 420.6.1.3.1 - specified concrete cover

q: What is the minimum concrete cover for concrete exposed to weather or ground, with No. 19 through No. 57 bars (NSCP 2015)?
n: Concrete exposed to weather or in contact with the ground needs 50 mm for No. 19 to No. 57 bars and 40 mm for No. 16 and smaller.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 420.6.1.3.1 - specified concrete cover

q: How long should new concrete or plaster generally cure before it is painted?
n: The usual rule is to wait about 28 days so the alkalinity and moisture drop and the paint bonds well.
ref: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 1032 - painting works, curing before painting

q: What is the minimum specified concrete compressive strength f'c for general structural concrete under NSCP 2015?
n: NSCP 2015, following ACI 318-14, sets 17 MPa as the general minimum f'c for structural concrete, and 21 MPa for members of special seismic systems.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 419.2.1.1 - minimum specified compressive strength

q: What does a higher R-value in roofing insulation indicate?
n: R-value measures thermal resistance, so a higher R-value means the roof slows heat flow better.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015 IRR of PD 1096), Building Envelope - roof insulation and thermal resistance

q: Which roof color generally has the highest Solar Reflectance Index (SRI)?
n: White and other light colors reflect the most sunlight and emit heat well, so their SRI is the highest.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015 IRR of PD 1096), Building Envelope - roof Solar Reflectance Index

q: What is the function of sag rods in a roof framing system?
o: Tie the columns to the footings
Support the purlins against sagging or lateral deflection along the roof slope
Hold roofing sheets to the purlins
n: Sag rods tie the purlins together along the slope and carry the component of load parallel to the roof surface, which keeps the purlins from sagging sideways.
ref: ASEP Steel Handbook - purlins and sag rods; NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15) - roof framing

q: Which footing type suits a steeply sloping site?
n: A stepped footing follows the slope in horizontal steps.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - foundations, stepped footings

q: Which foundation suits a weak soil with heavy loads, spreading the load over the entire building footprint?
n: A mat foundation spreads the loads over a large area to reduce bearing pressure and differential settlement.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - foundations, mat (raft) foundations

q: Which foundation type is used when the soil near the surface is very soft and a firm stratum lies at depth?
n: Piles transfer the loads through soft soil to a firm layer or by skin friction.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - foundations, pile foundations

q: Under the current Philippine standard, what is the minimum net-area compressive strength of a loadbearing concrete masonry unit?
n: PNS ASTM C90:2019 sets 13.8 MPa (2,000 psi) on the net area as the average of three units. It cancelled PNS 16:1984, which had required only 700 psi for loadbearing blocks, so older reviewers still give that figure.
ref: PNS ASTM C90:2019 - loadbearing concrete masonry units (cancels PNS 16:1984)

q: What minimum average thermal resistance must roof insulation provide under the Philippine Green Building Code?
n: Buildings covered by the Code must have roof insulation giving an average R-value of at least R-8. The Code allows no exception to this.
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Building Envelope - roof insulation

q: What is the longest commercially available length of deformed steel bars in the Philippines?
n: Deformed bars are rolled in standard lengths of 6.0, 7.5, 9.0, 10.5 and 12.0 m, so 12.0 m is the longest stock length.
ref: PNS 49 - deformed steel bars for concrete reinforcement, standard lengths

q: Which steel section is the one commonly used for roof purlins?
n: Cold-formed C-channel sections are the usual purlins. Sag rods tie them together along the slope.
ref: ASEP Steel Handbook - cold-formed sections, purlins
